findings.explanation: Splunkbase 4022 is 'Technical Addon for the Metricator application for Nmon (HEC)'. The ACI add-on is TA_cisco-ACI (Splunkbase 1897, deprecated in favour of Cisco DC Networking, 7777). The ID repeats in dataSources, implementation, detailedImplementation and references.
findings.suggested_fix: Cite Cisco DC Networking (7777) as the supported collector, with TA_cisco-ACI (1897, deprecated) as legacy, and remove every 4022 reference.

findings.explanation: SNMP and syslog destination groups (snmpGroup/snmpTrapDest, syslogGroup/syslogRemoteDest) are fabric-level external data collectors under uni/fabric, not tenant children. A tenant only references them through its monitoring policy's source objects, so an fvTenant rsp-subtree=full pull will not contain them. Step 3's 'Tenants → {tenant} → Settings' check for SNMP and syslog repeats the confusion.
findings.quote: child counts for `fvAp`, `fvBD`, `fvCtx`, `vzAny`, and any `monEPGPol`, **`monFabricPol`**, `snmpGroup`, `syslogGroup`, **`snmpTrapDest`**, **`syslogRemoteDest`** links reachable from the subtree
findings.suggested_fix: Describe the check as 'the tenant's monitoring policy has SNMP and syslog sources pointing at a destination group'. Confirm the source and relation class names in the APIC MIM, and validate under Admin → External Data Collectors.

findings.explanation: A vzAny that consumes and provides a permit-any contract is the classic permit-all shortcut, so 'consumed'/'provided' cannot mean restricted. The usual control is the VRF (fvCtx) policy-enforcement preference being 'enforced' rather than 'unenforced', plus a review of which contracts vzAny attaches.
findings.quote: fallback patterns treat `deny`, `restrict`, `consumed`, `provided` stances as compliant because they imply contracts rather than permit-all openness
findings.suggested_fix: Base the check on fvCtx enforcement (verify the attribute name, pcEnfPref) and on vzAny contracts whose filters are not permit-any. Stop treating 'consumed'/'provided' as compliant.

findings.explanation: These relation class names do not match the APIC relations I know of (for example fvRsTenantMonPol and fvRsAEPgMonPol).
findings.quote: confirm `monEPGPol` attachments referenced by **`fvRsMonBrIfPol`** / **`fvRsMonEPgPol`** style relations
findings.suggested_fix: Look up the tenant- and EPG-to-monitoring-policy relation classes in the APIC MIM and use the exact names.

findings.explanation: The saved-search name implies UC-18.1.15 (policy TCAM), but detailedImplementation says it belongs to UC-18.1.5 (tenant audit).
findings.quote: Pair alerts with **`aci_uc1815_tenant_audit_risk`** for change context.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename it to the UC-18.1.5 saved search (for example aci_uc185_tenant_audit_risk), or reference that UC's actual search name.

findings.explanation: The SPL returns any tenant with missing > 0, banded into priority tiers. ingest_skew > 600 only sets collector_lag_flag and does not page by itself.
findings.suggested_fix: Say the search lists every tenant failing at least one of the eight checks, with sev_high at 5+ missing and sev_med at 3+, and flags collector lag separately.

findings.explanation: Nothing in the UC (no hashing to an immutable store, no chain of custody) supports a legal-evidence claim.
findings.quote: retain raw **`cisco:aci:tenant_config`** JSON for attorney-ready snapshots
findings.suggested_fix: Say 'retain raw JSON as configuration evidence' and drop 'attorney-ready'.

findings.explanation: This link points to the Cisco homepage, and the 4022 reference links to an Nmon add-on.
findings.quote: "title": "Cisco APIC REST API Configuration Guide — Policy and Monitoring (Release 6.0(x))", "url": "https://www.cisco.com/c/en/us/"
findings.suggested_fix: Link the real APIC REST API Configuration Guide page, and replace 4022 with 7777 or 1897.

findings.explanation: An automated agent marked the UC verified, with no SME sign-off, while the object-location and add-on facts are wrong.

firewalled_field_flags.issue: tstats over datamodel=Change.All_Changes must reference fields with the dataset prefix (All_Changes.user, All_Changes.object, All_Changes.action). The query mixes `values(Change.object)` and `by Change.user Change.action Change.src` with an All_Changes.object filter, so the by-fields resolve to null and nothing is returned. The appended Inventory tstats has the same problem (Inventory.dest instead of All_Inventory.dest), and nodename=Change.All_Changes should be nodename=All_Changes.

vz_ok counts 'consumed'/'provided' vzAny stances as compliant, which also passes permit-any vzAny designs. snmp_ok/syslog_ok fall back to raw-text matches on 'snmpgroup'/'sysloggroup', which may never appear in tenant JSON (tenant monitoring policies reference destination groups by tDn, for example uni/fabric/slgroup-...), so these checks are likely always 0 or depend on undocumented normaliser fields.

summary: The tenant completeness checklist is a clear idea, but the UC names the wrong Splunkbase add-on and puts SNMP/syslog export objects inside tenant subtrees, which they are not. It treats vzAny contract consumption as proof of restriction, and its cimSpl references tstats fields with the wrong dataset prefix.
